solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drunk going after sailor covered in embarrassment (6)

indicatorNotes.going after: 'going after' means following in sequence, so the drunk's word is written behind the sailor's

annotation.surface: A sailor has had too much and is red-faced about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' sits first, tempting you to read it as an anagram signal; here it is a noun, a lush, and the order is fixed by 'going after'.
annotation.definitionFit: Ablush means blushing, red with embarrassment.

entries.clue: Feigned skill whenever in charge on vessel lacking leader (10)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: if = whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

annotation.surface: Someone only pretends to be competent when put in command of a ship that has no captain.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'vessel' is a small bottle, not a ship; the surface wants a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a feigned smile is put on rather than natural, the made-up quality the answer names.

entries.clue: Grasp king penguin’s tail (5)

indicatorNotes.tail: a word's tail is its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a king penguin by the tail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King penguin' is a real bird, so the two words read as one; they split, and the king is Lear.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the mental sense: to grasp a subject is to take it in and master it.

entries.clue: Locate suite at complex … (7)

indicatorNotes.complex: a complex arrangement of the letters

annotation.surface: Read with 5 down: finding a suite of rooms at a building complex, a short time after a company event.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 5 down for the surface only; each clue solves alone. 'Complex' looks like a noun, a building, but it works as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To situate something is to locate it, put it in place.

entries.clue: Need soft footwear skipping metres over boards (8)

indicatorNotes.skipping: to skip something is to leave it out, so the footwear leaves out the letter for metres
indicatorNotes.boards: to board is to take on as a passenger, so the shortened footwear carries the O inside it

annotation.surface: A shopper needs soft shoes for walking on floorboards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boards' looks like floorboards in the surface; it means takes on board. Need is the noun: there's no occasion for that.
annotation.definitionFit: Occasion can mean need or reason, as in 'no occasion to worry'.

entries.clue: … short time after company function (5)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means later in sequence, so the short time is written behind the company

annotation.surface: Read with 3 down: arriving at a suite in a complex shortly after a company event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a party after the company; it is the mathematical kind, cosec being the cosecant in trigonometry.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cosecant, one over the sine, is one of the trigonometric functions.

entries.clue: Had to host pre-eminent goddess (7)

indicatorNotes.to host: ATE holds STAR inside, as a host holds a guest

blocks.note: star = pre-eminent, as in star pupil

annotation.surface: Someone was obliged to entertain the most important of the goddesses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had to' reads as 'was obliged to'; 'had' is ATE and 'to host' is the instruction. Astarte is the Phoenician goddess of fertility and war.
annotation.definitionFit: Astarte was a goddess of the ancient Near East.

entries.clue: Jam sandwich is in progress (9)

indicatorNotes.sandwich: IS is sandwiched between parts of IMPROVE

annotation.surface: A jam sandwich is being made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jam sandwich' is lunch, but jam is the musicians' verb, and 'sandwich' tells you to put IS in the middle of IMPROVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Musicians who jam improvise together.

entries.clue: One informing on mobster regularly (4)

blocks.note: the even letters of ON MOBSTER: oN mObStEr

annotation.surface: Someone keeps passing information about a gangster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word, but its N starts the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A nose is slang for a police informer.

entries.clue: Fighter possibly is not prepared for scrap (8)

indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters of IS NOT are made ready in a new order

blocks.note: a fighter plane is one example of a jet

annotation.surface: A boxer is not ready for a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: The fighter is a warplane, not a boxer, and a scrap here means throwing away rather than a brawl.
annotation.definitionFit: To jettison something is to scrap it, throw it overboard.

entries.clue: Rat tailed others entering properties (9)

indicatorNotes.tailed: REST has its tail, the last letter, cut off
indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go into, so the docked others go inside the properties

blocks.note: REST (the others) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A rat followed other rats into some buildings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' reads as followed, which suits a rat; it means docked. 'Properties' are qualities, not houses.
annotation.definitionFit: A rat is a traitor, and a traitress is a female traitor.

entries.clue: American blocks suppliers of water and provisions from abroad (5)

indicatorNotes.blocks: A sits in the middle of TAPS, blocking it

annotation.surface: A US company stops foreign firms from supplying water and food.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is trade policy; the definition is a plate of Spanish snacks.
annotation.definitionFit: Tapas are Spanish snacks, food from abroad.

entries.clue: Book craftsman to fix up the wall (9,2,3)

indicatorNotes.up the wall: up the wall means crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A craftsman is booked to repair a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as a verb, hire; it is the noun, Roald Dahl's children's novel. 'Up the wall' is British for crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Fantastic Mr Fox is a children's book by Roald Dahl.

entries.clue: Dog with rare name I misspelled (10)

indicatorNotes.misspelled: the letters are spelt in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A dog has an unusual name that I spelt wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: A Weimaraner's name really is often misspelt, which is the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: The Weimaraner is a German hunting dog breed.

entries.clue: Thicket gets dense at far end (5)

indicatorNotes.at far end: the letter at the far end of DENSE

annotation.surface: A thicket grows denser towards its far side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets' reads as becomes; it is cops, slang for catches.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a thicket is a dense clump of small trees and shrubs, the same small wood the answer names.

entries.clue: Bill after consuming port coming later (9)

indicatorNotes.after consuming: POSTER having consumed RIO holds it inside

blocks.note: a bill is a poster, as in billboard

annotation.surface: The bill arrives after the port has been drunk, at the end of a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill and port suggest dinner and a drink; they are a poster and Rio.
annotation.definitionFit: Posterior means later in time or order.

entries.clue: Hidden source of information very involved in leak (9)

indicatorNotes.source of: the source of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.involved in: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so I and V sit within the leak

blocks.note: to secrete is to ooze, leak

annotation.surface: A secret informant is caught up in a leak.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is spies and leaks; 'leak' is the verb secrete, to ooze.
annotation.definitionFit: Secretive can mean hidden or kept close, as in a secretive deal.

entries.clue: Convey ambassador around centre of Prague Old Town (8)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so the ambassador's letters wrap round the heart of the city

blocks.note: HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title

annotation.surface: An ambassador is driven round the middle of Prague's Old Town.
annotation.walkthrough: Prague's Old Town is a real district, so 'Old Town' seems part of the city; it is the definition, ancient Carthage.
annotation.definitionFit: Carthage was an ancient city in North Africa.

entries.clue: A second-rate marker, one that’s dry (9)

blocks.note: something that stains leaves a mark

annotation.surface: A cheap pen has run out of ink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' suits a pen with no ink; here it is a teetotaller.
annotation.definitionFit: A dry person does not drink alcohol, an abstainer.

entries.clue: Not all eland, antelopes moving slowly (7)

indicatorNotes.Not all: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: Some of the eland and other antelopes are ambling.
annotation.walkthrough: Andante is the musical direction for a walking pace.
annotation.definitionFit: Andante in music means at a moderately slow, walking pace.

entries.clue: Pick horror film in which lead character is axed (5)

indicators: in which lead character is axed

indicatorNotes.in which lead character is axed: the first letter of SCREAM is chopped off

blocks.clueFragment: in which lead character is axed

annotation.surface: Choose a horror film where the main character is killed with an axe.
annotation.walkthrough: In a horror film the lead being axed is the plot; here the lead is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its pick, the best part.

entries.clue: Pigment in narcotic cut out (7)

indicatorNotes.cut: NARCOTIC is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.out: the remaining letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A pigment has been removed from a drug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as drug slang for diluted; it docks the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Carotin (carotene) is the orange pigment in carrots.

entries.clue: Mock prosperous person that’s locked in East Georgian jail (4,2,3,5)

blocks.note: to send up is to mock

annotation.surface: Someone ridicules a wealthy man held in an eastern jail in the country of Georgia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' points not to the Caucasus but to the US state: send up the river is American slang for jail, from Sing Sing prison up the Hudson.
annotation.definitionFit: To send up the river is American slang for to jail someone.

entries.clue: Parking on part of motorway going north is punishable (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, P sits on top of the next piece
indicatorNotes.going north: in a down clue, the word reads upwards

annotation.surface: Parking on a northbound motorway lane carries a penalty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a traffic offence, so 'going north' seems like the direction of travel.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what is punishable carries a legal penalty, and the answer describes things relating to punishment.

entries.clue: See reflected parts through instrument (5)

indicatorNotes.reflected: LO is turned back to front

blocks.note: LO (see!, as in lo and behold) turned round

annotation.surface: Someone sees reflections through a telescope or similar instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun, components; it is a verb, splitting VIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a member of the violin family, a little larger than the violin.

entries.clue: Slip in auditorium building (4)

indicatorNotes.in auditorium: an auditorium is where things are heard

blocks.note: a social slip or blunder, whose French-looking spelling carries a silent final E

annotation.surface: Someone trips up in a theatre building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like part of 'auditorium building'; it stands alone. Gaff is British slang for a house or premises.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaff is British slang for a house or other building.

entries.clue: Foreign outsiders withheld from striking (5)

indicatorNotes.outsiders withheld from: the outer letters of SALIENT are kept back

blocks.note: the S and T at either end are dropped

annotation.surface: Foreign workers are barred from joining a strike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Striking' reads as on strike; it is the adjective, noticeable.
annotation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign, belonging elsewhere.

entries.clue: Man picked up work when unoccupied, covering for one retiring (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, heard
indicatorNotes.unoccupied: WHEN is emptied, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: a knight is a chess man
to go is to work, as in 'does it go?'

annotation.surface: A man took on extra work in his free time, filling in for a colleague who was retiring.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is office cover for someone leaving the job; 'retiring' means going to bed, and 'covering' is what you wear. Man is a chess piece, the knight.
annotation.definitionFit: A nightgown covers someone who is retiring for the night.

entries.clue: Gastropod devoured by winged beast earlier (8)

indicatorNotes.devoured by: what is devoured ends up inside the eater, so the gastropod goes within the winged beast

blocks.note: an ormer is an abalone, a sea snail

annotation.surface: A snail was eaten by a flying creature earlier on.
annotation.walkthrough: The winged beast sounds like a dragon; it is a humble fly.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as adverbs: 'earlier' and the answer both mean at a previous time.

entries.clue: Biased French article fine to broadcast (6)

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A slanted French newspaper piece is judged acceptable to go out on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' wants to join 'broadcast' as fair; it gives only F, and AIR comes from the broadcasting.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a biased referee favours one side, which is the opposite of even-handed.
